text:
anna-accounting: Incoming invoice from SeoulAI Ltd (file: invoice_2026-03-18_SA.pdf). Net amount: A33,500 (GBP), VAT: 0.00, total: A33,500. Vendor added a note: 'Korean WHT may apply; please gross-up per contract if withholding required'. They provided a scanned "Tax Residency Certificate" (CoTR) but it's in Korean. Can finance confirm next steps re: withholding / gross-up? cc @josh-fin-ops @rachel-legal

vendor-billing-bot: Invoice uploaded: invoice_2026-03-18_SA.pdf (inv_81234) and attachment CoTR_seoulai.pdf

josh-fin-ops: Thanks Anna. Two quick things: 1) Where is the paying entity based (UK Ltd vs Redwood US)? 2) Which contract / SOW are they referencing for the gross-up clause? Gross-up is unusual unless contract explicitly requires it.

emma-sales: They were engaged by EMEA product team. PO #EMEA-1147 issued to Redwood UK Ltd. Contract reference: Master Services Agreement v3.1, SOW ref SA-SOW-03. Vendor flagged clause 7.4 about "taxes and withholding" and pasted a snippet in their email.

rachel-legal: On tax: South Korea levies withholding on certain cross-border service payments to non-residents in some cases. But applicability depends on place-of-supply and treaty relief. If vendor provides a Certificate of Tax Residency (CoTR) from Korean tax authority and the payment source is UK, UK-Korea treaty may reduce/avoid Korean WHT, but the vendor must apply for relief or provide a valid CoTR plus form. We need an English translation of the CoTR or at least an extraction: name, tax year, issuing authority, and valid-until.

anna-accounting: Snippet from invoice:
```
Supplier: SeoulAI Ltd
Country: Republic of Korea
Invoice date: 2026-03-18
Description: Model fine-tuning and engineering support
Amount (GBP): 33,500.00
VAT: 0.00
Note: "Korean withholding may apply; vendor requests gross-up per contract clause 7.4"
```

josh-fin-ops: For AP coding, if we need to withhold, we'll apply tax_code: WHT_KOR (and the rate per table). But gross-up means we pay extra so vendor ends up with the net they expect. That's a commercial ask and must be contractually binding. If SOW/contract explicitly requires gross-up, procurement/legal must confirm. Otherwise we deduct withholding and remit.

procurement-team: Pulling the contract now. SOW SA-SOW-03 clause 7.4 reads: "Supplier shall be responsible for taxes in their jurisdiction unless Customer is required by law to withhold; in such case, Customer will pay an additional gross-up amount equal to the withholding to ensure Supplier receives the agreed net amount." It looks like a gross-up clause is present. Need legal sign-off.

rachel-legal: Confirmed clause exists. Next steps: 1) Validate CoTR authenticity (procurement/legal to request English translation or certified translation). 2) Determine whether Korean tax applies to payments from UK (likely no if services supplied remotely to UK company; but onsite days in London would complicate). 3) If we do withhold under Korean law, gross-up per clause 7.4 applies — but we need to document calculation and supporting tax advice.

emma-sales: Vendor said they had 3 onsite days in London in Jan. That could create UK-sourced income? They claim majority remote.

josh-fin-ops: For interim handling: hold payment for 3 business days and request the following from vendor: - certified English translation of CoTR - confirmation of number of UK days and dates - bank confirmation to accept gross-up payment (we need remittance instructions that include gross-up breakdown). We'll flag payment as PENDING_TAX_DOCS.

anna-accounting: I'll request those docs and pause payment. Draft message to vendor: "Please provide certified English translation of your Certificate of Tax Residency, confirm onsite dates, and confirm bank details for gross-up. Per contract clause 7.4, if withholding is required we will calculate the gross-up amount and remit accordingly once documentation is received." Shall I send?

rachel-legal: Yes send that. Also ask vendor to confirm if they've applied for Korean tax relief or have tax advisor memo. If they insist no withholding, ask for statutory basis/exemption.

procurement-team: Also uploading a copy of the contract clause to the ticket so AP can tag GL appropriately.

josh-fin-ops: If gross-up applies, AP will code two lines in payment file: one for grossed-up service fee, one for withholding remitted to SK tax authority. Example (for illustration only):
```
Service fee (net): 33,500.00 GBP
Withholding (assume 10%): 3,350.00 GBP
Gross-up amount payable by Customer: 3,350.00 GBP
Total remitted to Supplier: 36,850.00 GBP
```
We will require tax calculation backup and a signed vendor confirmation before paying the gross-up.

anna-accounting: Sent vendor message, uploaded to ticket. Vendor replied within hour: "We will provide certified translation and confirm onsite dates. We request payment by EOM and said they expect gross-up per contract." Attached vendor note.

emma-sales: We'll nudge them but emphasize we need docs to process.

rachel-legal: If they delay, we should not auto-accept gross-up claim. Keep payment on hold and escalate to CFO if needed. Also prepare to withhold and remit if vendor fails to substantiate.

josh-fin-ops: Noted. Setting AP flag: TAX_REVIEW_PENDING and provisional tax_code: WHT_POTENTIAL. Will update once CoTR translation and confirmation received.

anna-accounting: Closing checklist attached in thread: - Request certified English translation of CoTR (done) - Ask vendor to confirm onsite dates (done) - Procurement to confirm contract clause (done) - Legal to validate gross-up applicability (in progress) - Hold payment until signed confirmation and calculation provided (done)

vendor-billing-bot: Vendor message uploaded: seoulai_reply_2026-03-18.pdf

josh-fin-ops: I'll follow up with AP to ensure no payment gets released without TAX_REVIEW_PENDING cleared.

rachel-legal: Thanks all. Will update when we've reviewed the CoTR translation. If it's clean and shows Korean residency for FY2025 and vendor had UK PE or too many UK days, we may need tax advice. For now treat as HOLD. :no_entry_sign:
